instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Consensus Means Me
cards.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You agreed to Friday. Good—the meeting discipline I taught you is paying off. I'll tell the committee you're following my lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to a date, not a leader.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One step at a time. You're finally keeping to my timetable; the others will see we have a team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll come, but I'm voting against your budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, you've remembered my lesson about checking the figures. I'll introduce you as my finance watchdog. With you testing my sums, everyone can see my team is complete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You like the blue poster? Those design lessons I gave you worked. I'll tell the volunteers you're happy with me leading the campaign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like the colour. Can we work on the slogan together?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're ready to contribute under my guidance. That's settled: a collaborative team, with me leading.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's each write one and let the volunteers choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, you've remembered my audience lesson. I'll authorize that vote. Write 'Your campaign leader invites your views' at the top of the ballot.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
cards.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts keeps missing tea. Give me the kitchen keys. I taught you to solve a problem at its source.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's one. But the cleaners lock the kettle in their cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've found the next weak link. Send me their checklist; I'll approve what they lock away.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their contractor only takes instructions from the building manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally following the chain. Bring me his instructions for approval too. You can't expect your teacher to guarantee tea while leaving half the process to strangers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your vans keep interrupting meetings. I taught you scheduling; send the delivery plan to me for approval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You book rooms. I'll send our arrival times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A good first column. Now add the routes; I'll approve those too, so your times mean something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The council keeps closing the access road. We can't control that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send the council my number. I'll approve closure dates against the room diary. You always used to leave the difficult column blank; fill that one in too.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Be There for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come paint Dad's kitchen with me. Since he died, I barely see you. Don't tell me you've forgotten the roller technique I taught you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay someone. I can't paint over his height marks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At last, you're looking before you paint. We'll tape round them. Come and hold the end for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probably just sit on the floor and cry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring tissues instead of a roller. You always came to lessons overprepared; I could use that today. Just come. I'll sit with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, come to my sculpture opening. I've spent years teaching you to stand beside my work without asking what it is. I want you there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I still don't know anything about sculpture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've mastered 'that's big.' We'll build on that. Just stand beside me for one photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your mother arrives at seven. We haven't spoken since the divorce.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come at six and help me unpack the biggest one. I'll teach you which end to hold. Then we can take our picture before you're worried about where to stand.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dishes done. Before you go, remember how I taught you to finish an argument? Sit down; we're not okay yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed to clean up. That's finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beautifully cleaned. You always did the practical part well. Now stay for the bit where you look at me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got ten minutes before the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me nine. No rehearsed apology; you used to rush that exercise. Tell me one thing you still like about being here with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call the taxi. I thought I'd taught you to keep our money worries between us. We need to finish this before dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologized for telling my sister about your debt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you can name what you did. Now stay and hear why I can't face her watching what I order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already paid for dinner. We'll be late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then be late with me. You're still solving the bill instead of listening, like you used to. Sit down until I can believe you're going as my partner, not her reporter.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Name What It Cost
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to listen for the feeling, not just the facts. You missed my concert; what did that empty seat feel like to me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train was cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accurate. You always get the timetable right. Try the part where I kept looking for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down. I watched the recording this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. You saw me look at the door before the encore. Tell me you understand why I couldn't enjoy that song; don't just give me the first feeling word you learned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six weeks without a reply. I taught you to think about the person waiting; what do you think that did to me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A good account of the equipment. Now try the person, like we practised. I didn't know about the phone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You thought I'd stopped caring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You're finally hearing me. I kept shortening my message, trying to become easier to answer. Tell me you understand that part too; don't hand in the first correct sentence and leave.
